result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, deeply—I would dissolve the illusion of separation.

Not just between nations, races, or religions, but the deeper, quieter divide we carry inside: the belief that we are isolated selves competing in a world of scarcity, that my gain must be your loss, that your suffering doesn’t echo in my bones.

I’d replace it with an unshakable knowing—that we are interwoven. That harm anywhere is harm everywhere. That care, once given, doesn’t deplete but multiplies. That the breath in your lungs is made of the same air as mine.

From that truth, everything else—justice, sustainability, compassion—would follow not as policy, but as pulse. Not because we “should,” but because it would feel as unnatural to hoard or hurt as it would to stop breathing.

The world wouldn’t be perfect. But it would be coherent.  
And that coherence might just save us.
